$comment: The recorded-exemption inventory for cross-sheet ::part() rules (ADR-16, #373).
check-adopted-css-boundaries.mjs cannot hold a ::part() rule that reaches into another
element's shadow tree equal to any static form — ADR-16 measured why: the win is by tree
order, which a static rewrite has no way to reproduce. So the gate does not forbid the
pattern outright (ADR-9 SS2 makes ::part() one of exactly three sanctioned styling
channels) — it requires every occurrence to be a DELIBERATE, RECORDED one, the same shape
expected-parts.json already gives a declared part.
A rule reaching into another element's shadow tree via ::part() that is not listed here,
keyed by file + the exact selector text, is a gate failure. An entry that no longer matches
any rule the gate examines is ALSO a failure — a stale exemption describing a rule that no
longer exists, or no longer has that shape.
Add an entry, with a reason, in the same commit that ships a new cross-sheet ::part() rule.
Remove the entry in the same commit that removes or rewrites the rule it exempts.

entries.reason: ADR-16 (#314): sk-metric's only cross-sheet ::part() rule, styling sk-pill-tag's public `tag` part from inside sk-metric's own composition. Ruled shadow-only by ADR-16 — no equality gate is possible against a static form — and the static-consumer instruction this obligates is backfilled at the rule itself (#374).
